references.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Optimization Reference Manual, Volume 1

sections_pages.section: 20.3 AMX instruction throughput and latency; Table 20-2

notes: Table 20-2 lists TDP/* throughput 16 and latency 52 cycles; treat these as the manual's table entries, not an independently established application-level roof.
Section 20.5.2 gives MAX_TILE_K=64 for (u)int8 and 32 for BF16. Section 20.4 recommends 64-byte alignment for optimal performance and says not to align to 128/256-byte multiples.

Section 20.21 discusses low-precision expansions, integer decomposition, omitted low-significance products, and warns accuracy is not guaranteed. It does not validate this proposal's base-128 digits or exact error/overflow contract.

references.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 2B: Instruction Set Reference, M-U
notes: TDPB* encodings are all marked AMX_INT8. Operand tmm2 can be signed/unsigned according to the second pattern letter; tmm3 according to the third. The four variants are SS, SU, US, UU.

Operation pseudocode adds four byte products into each dword accumulator lane. Dword arithmetic is width-limited; do not rely on saturation. With the bounded candidate inputs, prove no signed overflow before invoking the instruction.
Tile memory operations use a base plus byte stride; consult the complete instruction exception/operand rules for implementation constraints.

references.title: Intel 64 and IA-32 Architectures Software Developer's Manual, Volume 2C: Instruction Set Reference, V
notes: Volume 2C covers V-Z; it does not contain the TDPB* entries. The signed/unsigned TDPB* instruction descriptions are in Volume 2B.
